item.title: Letter from the Newsletter Editor, July 2017
item.description: Hello everyone, Thanks to all of you who participated in our annual meeting in San Diego. We had a West coast record attendance of 1607 that included 79 SOBP travel awardees. The plenaries were outstanding, as were the symposia, oral, and posters. We continue to be the major scientific organization fostering the growth of the next generation of behavioral and clinical neuroscientists and the number of younger attendees was truly inspiring. item.title: July Newsletter – Mentorship Committee Commentary
item.description: The mentorship committee’s charge is to foster interest and enthusiasm for studying and conducting research in biological psychiatry in future generations. This past year, we have continued to provide mentorship to SOBP travel awardees in a number of groups including residents, graduate students, and junior faculty. item.description: Hello everyone, In this issue of our newsletter, we are pleased to announce the theme of our meeting in New York May 10-12, 2018: " Biomarkers, Biomodels and Psychiatric Disorders.” SOBP President Carol Tamminga and Chair of the Scientific Program Committee Lori McMahon chose this theme in order to use SOBP and the annual meeting to critically review and formulate emerging brain biomodels. item.title: SOBP Redelsheimer Distinguished Award
item.description: Purpose The SOBP Redelsheimer Distinguished Award was established by the Society of Biological Psychiatry to honor major breakthroughs in the field of biological psychiatry. This award is to recognize past research that has been completed and has contributed significantly to the advancement of biological psychiatry. Guidelines The award is a $50,000 cash prize and an engraved plaque. Because of the stature of this award it is recognized that it may not be awarded annually. Members and non-member
